access_continuity_justification: Honest answer: the project has one maintainer and no second person with commit or release access, so changes could not be merged and releases could not be published on the existing accounts within a week. Apache-2.0 permits an immediate fork and no private signing keys are needed (Sigstore keyless), but that continues the software under a different name. The two recognised remedies — a co-maintainer, or credential escrow with a will — are documented and neither has been arranged yet: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: soapbar is a library and produces no user interface. Its one user-facing surface, the documentation site, is built with MkDocs Material, which renders semantic HTML with keyboard-navigable navigation, skip links and light/dark themes with adequate contrast.
assurance_case_justification: A published assurance case with the threat model (assets, adversaries, attack surface), an explicit trust-boundary diagram, an argument that secure design principles were applied, and an argument that common implementation weaknesses are countered by static analysis, fuzzing, property-based testing and the conformance suite — including a residual-risk section: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/assurance-case/
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The full suite runs on every pull request and every push to main across Python 3.10-3.14 and reports pass/fail as a required status check: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr.yml
build_common_tools_justification: Builds use standard Python tooling: setuptools, pip, uv.
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tools (setuptools, pip, uv) are FLOSS.
build_justification: Standard PEP 517 build with setuptools produces wheels and sdists (uv build / python -m build).
build_non_recursive_justification: A single PEP 517 build (setuptools via uv build) driven by one pyproject.toml; there is no recursive per-directory build and therefore no cross-directory dependency ordering problem.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Pure Python: nothing is compiled or stripped, so there is no debugging information to preserve.
build_repeatable_justification: soapbar is pure Python: the source code is used directly rather than compiled, and the wheel is an archive of those same source files. No information is generated from source at build time.
build_standard_variables_justification: soapbar is pure Python with no native binaries; there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to be passed to.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1. This is stated plainly rather than argued around, together with what limits the damage and what would fix it: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant adopted and published in the standard location: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff runs on every pull request and push to main and fails the build on any violation, alongside mypy --strict; the configuration lives in [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names PEP 8 as the style guide, enforced through ruff (pycodestyle E/W and PEP 8 naming N), lists the additional rule sets, and states the one deliberate deviation (100-character lines): https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the required checks (pytest with a 93% coverage gate, ruff lint, mypy --strict) and the contribution conventions: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Signature, digest and canonicalisation algorithms are selectable per call (RSA-SHA256/RSA-SHA1, SHA-256/SHA-1, exclusive/inclusive C14N) with secure defaults and validation of the requested values; body encryption uses AES-256-GCM with legacy AES-256-CBC selectable on decrypt behind an explicit opt-in.
crypto_call_justification: All cryptography is delegated to the cryptography and signxml libraries and stdlib ssl; there are no custom implementations.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: TLS certificate verification is on by default (verify_ssl=True). Disabling it is an explicit, named opt-out; custom CA bundles are supported for private or government PKI roots and take precedence over the boolean.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: No credential or key is embedded in the source. Private keys and PKCS#12 bundles are supplied by the caller as file paths or in-memory bytes and are never written to disk or logged; server-side password lookup is an abstract validator hook, so the credential store belongs entirely to the deployer.
crypto_floss_justification: cryptography, signxml and OpenSSL are all FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Defaults meet NIST minimums: RSA-2048+, AES-256, SHA-256; the library generates no weak keys.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The library does not store credentials; UsernameToken transmission follows the WSS protocol (digest salted with a random nonce and timestamp).
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS is delegated to Python ssl/httpx, whose modern defaults prefer perfect-forward-secrecy cipher suites.
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms are used, via the cryptography and signxml libraries and stdlib ssl: XML-DSig with RSA-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, TLS.
crypto_random_justification: Security-relevant random values (WS-Security nonces) use secrets.token_bytes, a CSPRNG.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is provided by the Python ssl module through httpx; its defaults negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher, and soapbar sets no option that would lower this.
crypto_used_network_justification: All network communication is HTTPS. Request URLs are restricted to an http/https allowlist, TLS is delegated to httpx and the standard library ssl module, and the server warns at construction time when configured with a plain-HTTP service URL.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Verification is performed by httpx and the ssl module as part of the TLS handshake, which completes before any HTTP request line, header, cookie or WS-Security credential is transmitted.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: SHA-1 appears only where the OASIS WSS UsernameToken profile mandates it for interoperability, documented in SECURITY.md; all security-relevant defaults are SHA-256: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_working_justification: Security defaults depend on no broken algorithms (no MD4/MD5/DES/RC4): signing defaults to RSA-SHA256 and encryption to AES-256-GCM.
dco_justification: No Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off is required. The project is Apache-2.0, whose section 5 already supplies an inbound contribution term, and it has had no external code contributors to date. Requiring sign-off would add a policy that only the sole maintainer could break; it will be adopted if outside contributions begin.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution is via PyPI over HTTPS; pip and uv verify package hashes.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Packages are delivered over TLS with hash verification; there is no unhashed, unprotected delivery path.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks the uv dependency graph and the GitHub Actions weekly and opens grouped update pull requests, and the OpenSSF Scorecard Vulnerabilities check tracks known advisories: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: The README and the documentation site describe what soapbar does (SOAP client/server/WSDL library for Python) and the problem it solves: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge and the OpenSSF Scorecard badge, mirrored on the documentation site: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar#readme
documentation_architecture_justification: High-level design, component responsibilities and request flow: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/architecture/
documentation_current_justification: The documentation site is rebuilt and redeployed by CI on every change to docs/, mkdocs.yml or src/, and the API reference is generated from source docstrings with mkdocstrings, so it cannot drift from the code. No known documentation defects are outstanding.
documentation_interface_justification: The documentation site provides reference documentation for the public API (client, server, types, WSDL, faults, security): https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/
documentation_quick_start_justification: Quick start guide with a runnable server and client in a few lines: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/quickstart/
documentation_roadmap_justification: A roadmap covering the next twelve months, including an explicit table of what will not be implemented and why: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: Security requirements, trust model and limitations are documented in SECURITY.md and on the site, with a full assurance case: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/assurance-case/
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Property-based tests assert invariants at run time, and the fuzz harness treats any exception outside the documented error contract as a crash.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis findings are outstanding: the weekly Atheris runs have reported no crashes, and local runs of the same harness (hundreds of thousands of executions) found none.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Coverage-guided fuzzing with Atheris runs weekly in CI over all parsing entry points, complemented by Hypothesis property-based tests: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Python is a memory-safe language; the memory-unsafe surface lives in widely-vetted FLOSS dependencies (lxml/libxml2).
english_justification: All documentation, issues, commit messages and code comments are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are triaged and answered in the issue tracker.
external_dependencies_justification: Dependencies are declared machine-readably in pyproject.toml (PEP 621) and pinned with hashes in uv.lock; every release additionally ships a CycloneDX SBOM of the runtime dependency graph: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/pyproject.toml
governance_justification: Governance model, decision process and dispute resolution are documented: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardening_justification: The XML parser is constructed without entity resolution, DTD loading, network access or huge-tree support; message size and nesting depth are capped; unhandled exceptions are scrubbed before reaching a client; WS-Security verification fails closed without a caller-supplied trust anchor; and body encryption is authenticated. Threats and controls are mapped in the assurance case: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/assurance-case/
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles are applied and argued explicitly — fail closed, secure by default with named opt-outs, least authority for the parser, complete mediation before expensive operations, and economy of mechanism by delegating all cryptography: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/assurance-case/
input_validation_justification: Untrusted input is validated against allowlists before use: request URLs against an http/https scheme allowlist, request bodies against a size limit and a 100-level nesting-depth check performed before the document tree is built, WSDL imports against a no-fetch-by-default policy with a recursion cap, required operation parameters against the operation signature, and optionally the SOAP Body against the WSDL-embedded XSD.
installation_common_justification: Installed and uninstalled with the standard Python conventions: `pip install soapbar` / `pip uninstall soapbar`, or `uv add soapbar`. Optional feature sets are standard extras (soapbar[client], [security], [all]).
installation_development_quick_justifica: `git clone` followed by `uv sync --group dev --group lint --group type` installs the library, the test suite and the full check environment in one command, documented at the top of CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is handled by pip/uv, which honour the standard Python conventions for install location — the active virtual environment, --prefix, --target and --user.
interact_justification: The README and docs explain installation from PyPI and link GitHub issues for bug reports and enhancements, and CONTRIBUTING.md for contributions: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar
interfaces_current_justification: The test suite run with warnings enabled emits no DeprecationWarning or PendingDeprecationWarning; no deprecated standard-library or lxml APIs are used. The one deliberate exception is the opt-in RSA-SHA1 signing profile, reachable only when a caller explicitly requests it because SEFAZ NF-e mandates it, and documented as such in SECURITY.md.
internationalization_justification: soapbar is a library with no user interface, no CLI and no localizable message catalogue; the only human-readable strings are developer-facing exception messages, whose exact text is explicitly excluded from the public contract by STABILITY.md.
know_common_errors_justification: Common vulnerability classes (XXE, SSRF, injection, XML signature wrapping, entity-expansion and nesting DoS) are known and actively mitigated; see SECURITY.md and the 2026-07 audit fixes in the 0.13.0 release notes.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles: fail-closed defaults (trust anchors required for signature verification), least privilege, hardened XML parsing (XXE/DTD disabled), SSRF-safe WSDL import handling.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: frequent releases (0.15.4 in July 2026, 28 versions on PyPI), automated release pipeline, CI on every change, prompt issue and security responses.
maintenance_or_update_justification: SECURITY.md states the supported version line and the upgrade path, versioning follows SemVer under STABILITY.md, and every breaking change carries its migration in the CHANGELOG: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are stored in the repository; GitHub secret scanning is enabled.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Well above 50%: of the fix commits in the project's history, 43 of 64 (67%) added or changed tests in the same commit, and every security fix shipped with regression tests — the trust-anchor fix, authenticated encryption, the signature-coverage check, timestamp freshness and the local-file import restriction.
release_notes_vulns_justification: Release notes identify fixed vulnerabilities by advisory id, e.g. GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6 in the 0.13.0 entry of CHANGELOG.md.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
repo_interim_justification: The main branch holds interim versions between releases.
repo_public_justification: Public Git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar
repo_track_justification: Git tracks all changes; full history and pull request discussion are preserved on GitHub.
report_archive_justification: The GitHub issue tracker is a searchable public archive of reports and responses: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/issues
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted via the GitHub issue tracker, referenced from the README and CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/issues
report_responses_justification: The maintainer responds to submitted issues; see the tracker archive: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/issues
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md tabulates each role (maintainer, reviewer, security responder, release manager, CoC enforcer), its responsibilities and who holds it; review routing is enforced by .github/CODEOWNERS: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
signed_releases_justification: Every release is signed with Sigstore keyless provenance over the wheel, sdist and SBOM, attached to the GitHub release as a .sigstore.json bundle, and PyPI carries PEP 740 attestations from the same pipeline. There is no long-lived private key to protect: the signing identity is the release workflow via OIDC. The verification process is documented for users with a runnable gh attestation verify example: https://hitoshyamamoto.github.io/soapbar/security/#verifying-a-release
sites_password_security_justification: The project stores no passwords. The repository, issue tracker and downloads are hosted by GitHub and PyPI, and the documentation site is static GitHub Pages with no authentication.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: The CodeQL security-extended query pack specifically targets common vulnerability classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: All static-analysis findings are triaged promptly: fixed, or dismissed with a public written rationale in code scanning.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (security-extended queries) runs on every pull request and push to main, plus weekly; ruff with flake8-bandit rules and mypy --strict run in the same CI: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and every push to main, plus weekly scheduled runs.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Continuous integration runs on every pull request and every push to main — lint, strict type check, test matrix over Python 3.10-3.14, examples smoke tests (https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr.yml) and CodeQL (https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml). A branch ruleset requires PRs, so every change is checked.
test_invocation_justification: The whole suite runs with a single standard command, uv run pytest, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_justification: An automated pytest suite (989 tests, including Hypothesis property-based tests) runs in CI on every pull request and push to main.
test_most_justification: Coverage is 93.96% counting statements and branches together — the metric the 93% CI gate enforces; statement-only coverage is 95.69%.
test_policy_justification: The enforced 93% coverage gate means new functionality must ship with tests, and the frozen public-API snapshot test forces deliberate, reviewed API changes.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states as a formal requirement that new functionality must add tests in the same pull request and that bug fixes must add a regression test, and the pull request template carries a matching checklist item: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests-are-required
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is 95.7% (3753 of 3922 statements), measured by coverage.py in CI on every pull request.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent history shows tests added alongside functionality (e.g. the property-based suite in PR #113).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires running the suite with its coverage gate before opening a PR, which operationally requires adding tests for new code: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components are standard packages resolved from PyPI with version ranges in pyproject.toml; there are no vendored or bundled convenience copies, so a fixed upstream version is picked up by a normal dependency update.
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in Git (e.g. v0.15.4): https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are created by the automated release pipeline through the GitHub API and are not OpenPGP-signed. Release artifacts are instead signed with Sigstore keyless provenance bound to the workflow identity, which is verifiable without distributing a maintainer public key; see the release verification documentation.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version, published to PyPI and tagged in Git.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unfixed critical vulnerabilities; all 2026-07 audit findings were fixed in 0.13.0.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The only publicly known vulnerability (GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6) was fixed and released within days (0.13.0, 2026-07-03).
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: One vulnerability has been resolved in the last 12 months, GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6. It was found by the maintainer during an internal audit rather than reported externally, so there is no external reporter to credit; the published advisory records this: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/security/advisories/GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting (private security advisories) is enabled and is the documented channel: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: A private disclosure process is documented in SECURITY.md: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md documents the response process and targets (acknowledgement within 5 business days, initial assessment within 14 days) for a single-maintainer project; in practice the past advisory GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6 was fixed and released within days (0.13.0, 2026-07-03): https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: A documented private disclosure process with response targets, published in the standard location and surfaced through GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any lint or type warning; the tree is kept warning-free.
warnings_justification: ruff (including flake8-bandit security rules) and mypy --strict run in CI on every pull request and push to main.
warnings_strict_justification: mypy runs in --strict mode and ruff enforces an extensive rule set (E,F,W,I,N,UP,B,SIM,S,RUF).
